profile.headline: Associate Software Engineer - Capital One
profile.summary: Software Engineer at Capital One with a background in biotech project management. Experienced in leading projects and collaborating across teams, now applying the same rigor and problem-solving mindset to building scalable, high-quality software solutions.

positions.title: Project Manager
positions.description:
- Initiated and developed new projects through client engagement and Business Development efforts. 

- Established project parameters in internal tracking systems, ensuring budget accuracy and adherence to timelines.

- Served as the primary contact for clients throughout project lifecycle, addressing administrative inquiries and resolving issues related to study costs and invoicing.

- Monitored and tracked study progress to accurately recognize project revenue based on milestone achievements and revenue recognition principles.

- Collaborated with clients and Operations to manage project scope changes, facilitating necessary amendments and ensuring alignment with client requirements.

- Coordinated invoice milestones for studies, providing finance department with requisite documentation for client invoicing. Prepare comprehensive cost summaries and verify costs prior to project closure.

- Generated requested reports for Site or PM management, providing insights and data analysis as needed.

positions.title: Study Director | Associate Scientist
positions.description:
- Collaborated with various pharmaceutical clients by writing study protocols tailored to their research while abiding by the IACUC, ACUP, and technical operation limitations.

- Initiated projects with internal team, overseeing all steps and ensuring perfect execution of tasks.

- Scheduled tasks, inoculations, and procedures efficiently to accommodate the team’s schedule.
	
- Updated clients biweekly with study progress and participated in regular meetings.

- Organized studies well and successfully achieved deadlines among various phases ranging from: protocol drafting to finalization; study preparation; inoculation; monitoring of clinical observations, body weight, tumor volume of mice; dosing; study termination; and shipment of samples.  

- Demonstrated critical thinking and quick decision making when running studies in vivo. 

- Summarized key findings upon study completion in reports which were sent for client review.

positions.title: Junior Study Director | Study Coordinator
positions.description:
- Organized tasks for the many ongoing studies (varying from 20-40 client studies at a time), with each status ranging from: protocol drafting, protocol finalization, study preparation, daily study execution, monitoring of clinical observations/body weight/tumor volume, dosing, study termination, and shipment of collected tissues and/or drugs. 

- Proofread protocols from client studies and prepared for experiments using Study Director/Log. Also used Microsoft Excel and Word to create forms such as: cage cards, dosing calendar, tissue collection sheets, tube labels, and PK tables. 

- Scheduled inoculation dates, major milestones for studies, weekly team meetings, coverage of tasks, and daily checklists via Smartsheet for the Research Associates.

- Assigned studies to Research Associates based on the individual's workload and skill level. 

- Provided hands-on technical operational support (with mice) including: anesthetized syngeneic inoculations and syringe-loading, tissue collections and necropsies, processing blood for either plasma or serum, and general quality control of procedures. 

- Coordinated shipments with the Logistics Department in addition to creating forms (packing slips, box maps, shipping request forms) and performing quality control of said shipments. 
 
- Ordered items necessary for studies including tissue collection tubes and pharmaceutical drugs via Oracle. 

- Developed strong interpersonal and effective communication skills by working with various departments (Technical Operations, Scientific Operations, Cell Culture, Biodevelopment Marker Team, Logistics).

- Fully read SOPs and often referenced them for guidance or clarification purposes.

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher
positions.description:
- Currently conducting experiments observing the effect of corticosterone on LH pulses and activation of Kisspeptin/RFRP-3 neurons in mice. 

- Performed in-situ hybridizations, corticosterone ELISA assays, and tail-blood collections for the aforementioned experiments. Also utilized ultra-sensitive murine LH ELISA.

- Assisted in-situ hybridization procedures by preparing appropriate solutions, transferring racks, creating radioactive probe, cover-slipping, developing and fixing slides, and cleaning radioactivity with count-off. 

- Laboratory skills include: polymerase chain reactions (PCRs), gel electrophoresis, coronal brain cutting, tail digestions, DNA purification and extraction via DNeasy kit, nano-dropping, and counting mRNA expression. 

- In vivo experience with mice includes: castrating, handling for experiment habituation, collecting tail-blood, weaning, brain extracting, retro-orbital bleeding, ear tagging, tail clipping, vaginal smearing, and scruffing.

- Attended weekly lab meetings to discuss logistics, future experiments, scheduling, and general progress updates. Developed effective communication and strong teamwork skills. 

- Also attended weekly group meetings with other labs in the Reproductive Medicine Department to discuss recent advancements and papers in neuroendocrinology.

positions.title: Instructional Apprentice / Tutor
positions.locationName: UCSD (Dr. Su and Dr. Burg's BILD 2 courses)
positions.description:
- Led weekly discussion sections by teaching lecture material and answering questions.  

- Held office hours; accepted regrade requests, addressed logistical issues, or clarified biology concepts.
 
- Checked email and TritonEd daily to answer questions from students. 

- Graded midterms and final exams, all consisting of multiple choice and free response. 

- Course consisted of the following topics: nutrition, digestion, circulation, gas exchange, the immune system, renal function, endocrinology, reproduction, and the nervous system.

company.name: Teaching at University of California, San Diego
Undergraduate Research at University of California, San Diego

positions.title: Clinical Research Assistant
positions.description:
- Explored whether bright white light therapy can alleviate depressive moods in patients demonstrating symptoms of Stage B Heart Failure. 

- Collaborated with Research Coordinator in visiting patients at the Altman Clinical and Translational Research Institute.

- Guided participants with questionnaires (Including the Beck Depression Inventory Test) during in-person visits and explained details of the three-month study.

- Collected urine samples and circadian rhythm data from an Actiwatch Spectrum. 

- Monitored light books by regularly checking on the battery life and by activating them prior to patient assignment. 

- Shadowed psychiatrist and research coordinator when conducting a Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID) to test for major mental disorders such as depression, bipolar disorder, and PTSD. 

- Organized comprehensive SCID results onto Excel file. 

- Recruited senior patients via EPIC and ResearchMatch.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
- Administered a SONA study observing whether synchrony with an anonymous person may encourage prosocial behavior. 

- Analyzed data from the aforementioned study, and then revised the data collection method by using SurveyMonkey, focusing on hypothetical synchronous scenarios. 

- A third study involved randomizing the order of questions from SurveyMonkey. 

- Discussed research papers every week relevant to psychological phenomena like memory, synchrony, and attention -- with heavy emphasis on children data.

company.name: Volunteer Experience at University of California, San Diego

positions.title: Call Pool Volunteer
positions.description:
- Enhanced communication and interpersonal skills by aiding in miscellaneous tasks like transporting equipment, delivering lab specimens, discharging patients, and greeting guests at the front entrance.

- Immersed myself throughout the Thornton, Sulpizio, Perlman, and Jacobs Hospitals.

- Worked alongside other Call Pool Volunteers to divide tasks and collaborate when needed.

- Achieved approximately 150 hours of volunteer service.

positions.title: High School Tutor
positions.description:
- Tutored Integrated Math III, which included algebra, geometry, and probability.

- Connected with students ranging from 9th to 12th grade, approaching them in a friendly way while maintaining a professional attitude.

projects.title: Fetsy Shop Online
projects.description:
- Leveraged MongoDB-Express-React-Node.JS (MERN) stack technologies inspired by an Etsy Shop (DigiWitz) to minimize Etsy fees and maximize potential profits.

- Utilized Passport to implement secure session management, enabling seamless admin authorization for shop management (creating, editing, deleting products; oversee all Reviews and Orders) and user authentication for online shopping (adding items to Cart or Favorites, buying products, accessing Orders, leaving Reviews). 

- Demonstrated React proficiency by efficiently structuring components and utilizing hooks (useState, useEffect, useContext) to create intuitive, responsive user interfaces.

- Employed Fetch API and async/await functions in JavaScript to handle HTTP requests, which were primarily handled by Axios. 

- Managed image assets with Cloudinary and orchestrated data flow to MongoDB via Mongoose, namely for secure storage and management of sensitive information.

- Explored usage of JSON Web Tokens (JWT's) initially, but for security purposes switched to session management.

- Hashed and salted passwords securely via Bcrypt; session IDs were stored in the client's cookies and destroyed when logged out.

- Maintained consistent version control through regular commits to Git throughout the coding process.

- Implemented CSS concepts such as flexbox, relative and absolute positioning, media queries for page responsiveness. Also utilized Bootstrap via Reactstrap.

- Deployed project onto Render. Initially tested backend routes via Postman.

projects.title: Board Games Galore
projects.description:
- Developed MERN project inspired by the Board Game Geek website, emphasizing proficiency in the Board Game Atlas (BGA) API and integration of server-side data through Fetch API.

- Enhanced React expertise by integrating diverse components, useState for state management, useEffect to manage side effects such as Fetch API calls, React Router DOM for routing, and Navbar.

- Implemented async/await functions alongside promise and error handling mechanisms for managing GET requests (BGA API) and handling various HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) for server-side data. Leveraged Abort Controller for seamless cancellation of asynchronous fetch calls as per user requirements.

- Incorporated MongoDB for efficient non-image data storage, defining comprehensive schemas for document structures and regulations, and integrating models to facilitate interaction with MongoDB for operations such as document creation, searching, updating, and deletion.

- Employed Cloudinary for streamlined image storage needs, transitioning from Multer to Cloudinary to ensure scalability and efficiency.

- Honed CSS skills by utilizing advanced techniques such as flexbox layouts, Bootstrap framework, relative and absolute positioning, z-index manipulation, and effective CSS selector usage.
